root.label: Inheritance & Virtuals
root.note: C++ separates embedded subobject layout and compile-time lookup rules from runtime virtual dispatch.

children.label: Object Layout
children.note: Derived objects embed base subobjects contiguously in memory rather than holding hidden heap pointers.

children.label: Embedded Base Subobject
children.note: Every Derived instance stores its Base subobjects directly inside its own footprint.

children.label: Object Slicing
children.note: Passing Derived by value copies only the Base subobject and resets the dynamic type to Base.

children.label: Pointer Adjustment
children.note: Converting a non-null derived pointer to a secondary base shifts the address by that base offset.

children.label: Virtual Bases
children.note: Virtual inheritance merges diamond bases into one subobject initialized by the most-derived class.

children.label: Virtual Dispatch
children.note: Polymorphic classes select overriders at runtime using the dynamic type rather than the pointer type.

children.label: Static vs Dynamic Type
children.note: Expressions carry a fixed compile-time static type while pointers and references point to a dynamic type.

children.label: vptr and vtable
children.note: Each polymorphic object holds a vptr pointing to its class vtable of virtual function entries.

children.label: override and final
children.note: These specifiers catch signature mismatches at compile time and enable devirtualization.

children.label: Pure Virtual Functions
children.note: Marking a virtual function pure makes the class abstract while still allowing a qualified definition.

children.label: Lookup & Access
children.note: Name hiding, access specifiers, and default arguments resolve statically before virtual dispatch runs.

children.label: Name Hiding
children.note: Declaring any same-named member in Derived hides all Base overloads unless brought in with using.

children.label: Static Access Check
children.note: Access rules on a virtual call are enforced against the static type at the call site.

children.label: Static Default Args
children.note: Default argument expressions come from the static receiver type even when a derived override executes.

children.label: Lifetime Boundaries
children.note: Polymorphic deletion and constructor or destructor execution obey strict dynamic-type boundaries.

children.label: Virtual Destructors
children.note: Deleting Derived through a non-virtual Base destructor is undefined behavior rather than a partial free.

children.label: Ctor and Dtor Dispatch
children.note: During Base construction or destruction the object's dynamic type is Base, preventing derived dispatch.

children.label: RTTI & Casts
children.note: Runtime type identification inspects polymorphic objects for safe downcasts and cross-casts.

children.label: dynamic_cast
children.note: Navigates polymorphic hierarchies safely, returning null for invalid pointers or throwing bad_cast for references.

children.label: typeid Operator
children.note: Evaluates the dynamic type_info for dereferenced polymorphic pointers and throws bad_typeid on null.
